newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro shares off lows, massively traded.
newsitem.headline: Jinro shares off lows, massively traded.

text.p: Shares of South Korea's troubled liquor maker, Jinro Ltd, recovered from early falls on Friday morning in what brokers described as panic buying in the hope of quick profits, brokers said.
The stock was trading at 7,250 won, down 440 won on the day, after falling to this year's lowest level of 7,080.
The stock topped the morning's actives list, with 1.48 million shares changing hands, against just 9,970 shares traded for the whole of Thursday.
Brokers said the buying was not driven by any improvement in the financial situation of the troubled company or its parent group, which has piled up 3.2 trillion won in debt.
"Institutions are selling and individuals are buying. Buyers appear to believe they can make money by buying at the current price level," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
Jinro's current price reflects a 62 percent drop from this year's highest level of 19,000 won at the start of 1997.
